page: Microsoft Azure FX12mds is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine instance operating under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs paired with 252.0 GB of system memory. This specific allocation establishes an unusually dense ratio of 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, addressing scenarios that demand significant working memory per thread while retaining dedicated execution resources without graphical processing acceleration.

Storage provisions for the FX12mds include 541 GB of bundled local solid-state drive (SSD) capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The local SSD provides rapid transient disk access for scratch data, operating system paging, and cache tiers. Network provisioning includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, requiring standard virtual network interface configuration and associated routing resources for external network connectivity.

From a cost and architecture perspective, the FX12mds targets high resource density per core. Because the vCPU allocation remains modest at 12 cores while RAM reaches 252.0 GB, operational expenditure is focused on high-memory density rather than massive parallel compute scaling. Tradeoffs include the absence of hardware accelerators such as GPUs and reliance on a standard 12-core ceiling for concurrent processing tasks.

Given its high RAM-to-vCPU allocation, bundled local SSD space, and dedicated Intel x86_64 compute cores, the FX12mds is targeted at large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), medium-scale analytics jobs, and batch memory-bound engineering workloads.
